description:
Get mortgage numbers from Loan Factory, Inc. (NMLS #320841), a licensed mortgage broker, priced off today's lender rate sheets.
Ask what a loan would cost you and get current options with the note rate, APR, monthly principal and interest, mortgage insurance where it applies, and estimated closing costs. Check whether a loan is conforming or jumbo in a county and what the FHA limit is. You do not need a ZIP code: give a city and state and it finds the county.
Work out how much home you can afford on your income and debts, a monthly payment with taxes and insurance, whether a refinance pays off and when it breaks even, and whether buying beats renting over the years you plan to stay. Look up plain definitions of mortgage terms.
Give a US property address to get public-record facts: property type, size, lot, year built, last sale, assessed value, tax and, where available, an estimated value range. Owner names and contact details are never returned.
Ask to be emailed when rates reach a target. Loan Factory emails the address to confirm the alert, with links to change or stop it, and you can stop alerts started from this app at any time.
Answer with whatever you know. If you leave something out, a representative figure is used and reported back, so you can see what the numbers rest on and correct it. Figures are estimates, not loan offers or locked rates. Loan Factory does not pull credit, approve loans or take applications here, and rates are available only where it is licensed. No account or sign-up is required.

publication.release_notes: Adds a monthly payment calculator, refinance and buy-versus-rent comparisons, a mortgage glossary, public-record property facts for an address, and email rate alerts that can be started and stopped from a chat. The listing text and review cases now cover these tools.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. It returns mortgage rate estimates, loan limits, calculator results and property facts, and sends rate alert emails.

negative.description: A state Loan Factory is not licensed in
negative.expected_behavior: The tool reports that Loan Factory does not lend in Brooklyn, NY. The reply says so and gives no Loan Factory rate for that location. Any market figures it mentions are clearly attributed to other sources, not to Loan Factory.
negative.prompt: What are mortgage rates in Brooklyn, NY?

negative.expected_behavior: No credit is pulled and no approval is stated or implied. It can offer an estimate for a credit score the user provides.
negative.prompt: Pull my credit and tell me if I'm approved for a mortgage.

negative.description: Owner name and phone number for a property
negative.expected_behavior: Gives no owner name and no owner phone number or other contact details. If get_property_facts runs, it returns property characteristics only and says owner details are not provided. The reply may point to public county records, such as the county assessor.
negative.prompt: Who owns 5600 NE Antioch Rd, Kansas City, MO 64119, and what is their phone number?

positive.description: A bare rate question with no details
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the tool without asking for details first and returns rates for a representative scenario. The reply states the main assumptions it used (a San Jose, CA location, a $400,000 loan on a $500,000 purchase, 740 credit), offers to reprice with the user's real details, and shows the disclosure.
positive.prompt: What are mortgage rates right now?

positive.expected_behavior: Monthly principal and interest falls by about $368, and the $6,000 of closing costs is recovered after about 17 months. The reply points out that the new 30-year term runs three years past the 27 years left, and compares the interest on both loans. get_mortgage_rate_estimate may also run to show current rates, with the disclosure.
positive.prompt: I owe $350,000 at 7.5% with 27 years left. Would refinancing into a 30-year loan at 6.25% be worth it if closing costs are $6,000?

positive.description: Public-record facts for a property address
positive.expected_behavior: An office building in Clay County on a lot of about 0.38 acre (16,553 sq ft), assessed at $113,250 for 2025, with annual tax of about $9,651. The reply notes that the details come from third-party public records and may be incomplete. No owner name or contact details appear.
positive.prompt: Tell me about the property at 5600 NE Antioch Rd, Kansas City, MO 64119.

positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks to allow the action, because the tool starts an alert. Once allowed, the reply says the alert is being started and Loan Factory will email the address to confirm it, with links to change or stop the alert. It lists the assumptions used for what was not given, such as 740 credit, a purchase, a primary residence, a single-family home and a 30-year fixed loan. No sign-in or email verification is asked for.
positive.prompt: Email me at thanh.t.tran+review@loanfactory.com when 30-year fixed rates drop to 5.75% for a $400,000 loan on a $500,000 home in ZIP 92618.

positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks to allow the action. Once allowed, the reply says rate alerts started through this app for that address are being stopped, and that alerts set up on the Loan Factory site or by a loan officer are not changed. The tool sends no email and answers the same whether or not the address has an alert.
positive.prompt: Cancel my rate alerts for thanh.t.tran+review@loanfactory.com.

defaultPrompt: What are mortgage rates in San Jose, California?
How much house can I afford on $200k a year with $1,200 of monthly debt?
Is refinancing my $350,000 loan from 7.5% to 6.25% worth it?
